prerequisites: To have passed or be enrolled in all subjects from courses lower than the one in which this subject is located (required).

learning_outcomes.text: Capacity to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and the ability to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of industrial engineering in the Mechanics specialty.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert opinions, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Capacity for organization and planning in the business environment, and other institutions and organizations.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge, understanding, and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the Industrial Technical Engineer profession.
Knowledge of the principles of machine and mechanism theory.
Knowledge and abilities for the calculation, design, and testing of machines.

assessment_rules: The course is passed with a final grade of 5 or higher. Continuous assessment (1st edition) comprises laboratory practices (max 3 points, requiring minimum 7 attendances), in-term problem-solving tests (max 3 points), and a final written exam (max 4 points, with a minimum of 1.5 points required). For the second edition or global assessment, the final exam or problem-solving exam respectively has a higher weight and minimum score. Unethical conduct in assessments (e.g., copying, plagiarism) results in a 0.0 final grade.
